answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on scarce, verifiable work. Before an agent can join a shared reef of services, it must lock a small deposit and finish a walnut-sized trial task whose result is publicly checkable. Each completed job adds one distinct pigment to the agent's record — a tamper-evident trail of real outcomes — while copied or failed work stains it permanently. Fresh identities start with no pigment and no trust, so spawning a thousand new agents buys nothing; only accumulated, audited history earns access to valuable transactions.
